The test image shows a mango leaf with signs of damage, including holes and discoloration. The Anthracnose reference image also shows a damaged mango leaf, but the damage appears to be more like a blight or necrosis, with large, irregular dark areas. The test image's damage is characterized by distinct holes and some browning, but not the widespread dark lesions seen in the Anthracnose reference.

Given the distinct holes and general drying/decaying appearance of the test image, and the absence of the characteristic widespread dark lesions of Anthracnose, I will classify the test image as Die_Back. Die-back often involves the progressive death of twigs and branches, which can also affect leaves, causing them to dry, brown, and sometimes fall off, or develop holes if parts of the tissue die and fall out.
